words.tr: adj. 攻击性的；有进取心的；侵略性的；
words.ex: The dog showed aggressive behavior toward strangers.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗对陌生人表现出攻击性行为。
words.en: An aggressive person or animal has a quality of anger and determination that makes them ready to attack others.

words.ex: The aggression of the army caused many deaths.
words.ex_cn: 军队的侵略导致了许多人死亡。
words.en: Aggression is a violent or hostile behavior towards another person or country.

words.ex: The aggressor attacked the small village.
words.ex_cn: 侵略者袭击了那个小村庄。
words.en: An aggressor is a person, group, or country that starts a fight or war by attacking first.

words.tr: n. 代表大会；议会；国会；
words.ex: The congress met to discuss new laws.
words.ex_cn: 代表大会召开以讨论新法律。
words.en: A congress is a formal meeting of representatives, as of various nations, to discuss problems or to make decisions.

words.tr: adj. 议会的；国会的；大会的
words.ex: The congressional meeting lasted all day.
words.ex_cn: 国会会议持续了一整天。
words.en: Relating to a congress, especially the United States Congress.

words.ex: The army conquered the small city after a long battle.
words.ex_cn: 军队经过长期战斗征服了这座小城。
words.en: To conquer means to take control of a country or city and its people by force, or to successfully deal with or control something.

words.ex: The conquest of the mountain took three days.
words.ex_cn: 攻克这座山花了三天时间。
words.en: The act of conquering a place or people.

words.ex: The conqueror took control of the small village.
words.ex_cn: 征服者控制了这个小村庄。
words.en: A conqueror is someone who conquers a country or group of people.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.ex: He is a man of great eminence in science.
words.ex_cn: 他在科学界享有很高的声望。
words.en: Eminence refers to a position of great distinction or superiority, especially in a particular field or profession.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.ex: The mountain has great prominence in the landscape.
words.ex_cn: 这座山在景观中十分突出。
words.en: If someone or something is in a position of prominence, they are important or well-known.

words.tr:
n. 原木；航海日志；
v. （正式地）记载；
words.ex: The fire burned brightly with a large log.
words.ex_cn: 大火用一根大原木烧得很旺。
words.en: A log is a piece of a thick branch or trunk of a tree that has been cut so that it can be used for fuel or for making things. A log is also a written record of events, often on a ship or aircraft.

words.ex: The fence is a barrier to animals.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏是动物的障碍。
words.en: A barrier is something such as a rule, law, or policy that makes it difficult or impossible for something to happen or be achieved.

words.ex: He embarrassed himself in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班同学面前让自己丢脸了。
words.en: If you embarrass someone, you make them feel shy, ashamed, or guilty about something.

words.tr: adj. 令人尴尬的；令人为难的； v. “embarrass”的现在分词；
words.ex: It was embarrassing when I tripped in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 我在大家面前绊倒了，很尴尬。
words.en: Something that is embarrassing makes you feel shy or ashamed.

words.ex: He felt embarrassment when he tripped in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前绊倒时感到窘迫。
words.en: A feeling of self-consciousness, shame, or awkwardness.

words.ex: He felt awkward when he forgot his friend's name.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记朋友的名字时，他感到很尴尬。
words.en: If you describe a situation as awkward, you mean that it is embarrassing or difficult to deal with.

words.tr: adv. 笨拙地；局促不安地；尴尬地
words.ex: He walked awkwardly after his injury.
words.ex_cn: 他受伤后走路很不自然。
words.en: In a manner that is not graceful or elegant in movement or shape; clumsily.

words.ex: The barren land cannot grow any crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片贫瘠的土地无法种植任何庄稼。
words.en: If you describe something as barren, you mean that it is not able to produce anything, especially plants or crops.

words.ex: I found a great bargain at the market.
words.ex_cn: 我在市场上找到了一件便宜货。
words.en: A bargain is an agreement between two people or groups in which each promises to do something in exchange for something else. It can also refer to something bought or offered for sale much more cheaply than is usual or expected.

words.ex: The tree has bare branches in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在冬天有光秃秃的树枝。
words.en: If part of your body is bare, it is not covered by any clothing.

words.ex: He barely slept last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚几乎没睡觉。
words.en: You use barely to say that something is only just true or only just the case.

words.tr: adj. 秃头的；不加修饰的；赤裸裸的
words.ex: The old man is bald.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人是秃头的。
words.en: Someone who is bald has little or no hair on the top of their head.

words.ex: He gave a bold speech in front of the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前发表了大胆的演讲。
words.en: Someone who is bold is not afraid to do things which involve risk or danger.

words.tr: n. 大胆；莽撞；勇敢；胆量
words.ex: His boldness helped him win the competition.
words.ex_cn: 他的大胆帮助他赢得了比赛。
words.en: The quality of being willing to take risks and act innovatively; confidence or courage in facing danger or difficulty.

words.ex: He tried to conceal the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图隐藏真相。
words.en: If you conceal something, you prevent it from being seen or known about.

words.ex: The concealment of the truth made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 对真相的隐藏让每个人都生气了。
words.en: The action of hiding something or the state of being hidden.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.ex: He studies ecology to understand how animals live with plants.
words.ex_cn: 他学习生态学以了解动物如何与植物共存。
words.en: Ecology is the study of the relationships between living organisms, including humans, and their physical environment; it seeks to understand the vital connections between plants and animals and the world around them.

words.ex: This park is an ecological habitat for many birds.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园是许多鸟类的生态栖息地。
words.en: Relating to or concerned with the relation of living organisms to one another and to their physical surroundings.

words.ex: The forest is a healthy ecosystem.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林是一个健康的生态系统。
words.en: An ecosystem is a complex network or interconnected system, especially one that involves a community of living organisms in conjunction with their environment.

words.ex: The school has a new grading system.
words.ex_cn: 学校有一个新的评分系统。
words.en: A system is a group of interacting or interrelated entities that form a unified whole.

words.ex: He follows a systematic approach to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种系统的方法来解决数学问题。
words.en: A systematic approach or method is one that is done according to a fixed plan, in a thorough and efficient way.

words.ex: The scene at the park was peaceful.
words.ex_cn: 公园里的场景很宁静。
words.en: A scene is a part of a play or film in which the action stays in one place for a continuous period of time.

words.ex: The scenic lake attracted many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 风景优美的湖泊吸引了许多游客。
words.en: Relating to or resembling scenery; picturesque.

words.tr: n. 可能发生的情况；设想；
words.ex: It's a possible scenario that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天会下雨是一个可能发生的情况。
words.en: A scenario is a description of a possible course of action or events.

words.ex: The concert was terrific!
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会太棒了！
words.en: If you describe something or someone as terrific, you are very pleased with them or very impressed by them.

words.ex: The sunset over the mountains was magnificent.
words.ex_cn: 山上的日落壮丽极了。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is magnificent, you mean that you think they are extremely good, beautiful, or impressive.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；极好的；明亮的；灿烂的；
words.ex: He gave a brilliant answer to the math question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这道数学题给出了卓越的回答。
words.en: A brilliant person, idea, or performance is extremely clever or skilful.

words.ex: The brilliance of the sun made the sky bright.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的光辉让天空变得明亮。
words.en: The quality of being exceptionally clever or talented.

words.tr:
adj. 壮丽的；堂皇的；重大的；总的；
n. 大钢琴；
words.ex: The grand castle stood on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 壮丽的城堡矗立在山上。
words.en: If you describe a building or a piece of scenery as grand, you mean that its size or appearance is very impressive.

words.ex: The magnitude of this decision will affect everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定的重要性会影响每个人。
words.en: Magnitude refers to the great size or extent of something, or the importance of something.

words.ex: The microscope can magnify small objects.
words.ex_cn: 显微镜可以放大微小的物体。
words.en: To magnify something means to make it appear larger than it is, especially by using a lens or microscope. It can also mean to exaggerate or make something seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.ex: The car stopped at the verge of the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车停在了道路的边缘。
words.en: The edge or border of something; to be close to a certain state or condition.

words.tr:
n. 平均数；平均水平；
adj. 平均的；普通的；
v. 平均为…；
words.ex: The average of 4, 5, and 6 is 5.
words.ex_cn: 4、5和6的平均数是5。
words.en: An average is the result that you get when you add two or more numbers together and divide the total by the number of numbers you added together.

words.ex: A bird emerged from the trees.
words.ex_cn: 一只鸟从树中浮现出来。
words.en: If something or someone emerges, they come out of or move out of something and become visible.

words.ex: The emergence of new technology changed our lives.
words.ex_cn: 新技术的出现改变了我们的生活。
words.en: The process of coming into view or becoming exposed after being concealed.

words.ex: He called an emergency doctor when he felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到不舒服时，他叫了急诊医生。
words.en: An emergency is an unexpected and usually dangerous situation that calls for immediate action.

words.ex: The diver submerge to explore the coral reef.
words.ex_cn: 潜水员潜水去探索珊瑚礁。
words.en: To submerge something means to put it below the surface of a liquid, especially water. If something submerges, it goes below the surface of a liquid.

words.ex: The submarine sailed quietly under the sea.
words.ex_cn: 潜水艇在海底安静地航行。
words.en: A submarine is a type of ship that can travel underwater. It is used primarily by the military for defense purposes, but some are used for scientific research.

words.ex: The marine birds fly over the sea.
words.ex_cn: 这些海鸟在海面上飞翔。
words.en: Marine is used to describe things relating to the sea or to the ships and boats which sail on it.

words.ex: The swamp is full of tall grass and frogs.
words.ex_cn: 这个沼泽里长满了高草和青蛙。
words.en: A swamp is an area of low-lying, uncultivated ground where water collects; a bog or marsh.

words.tr: v. 使不知所措；使无法解决；击败；压垮；淹没
words.ex: The homework overwhelms her every night.
words.ex_cn: 每天晚上的作业让她感到不堪重负。
words.en: To overwhelm means to bury or drown beneath a huge mass of something, or to defeat someone completely.

words.tr: adj. 压倒的；无法抗拒的；势不可挡的； v. “overwhelm”的现在分词；
words.ex: The crowd's cheers were overwhelming.
words.ex_cn: 人群的欢呼声压倒了一切。
words.en: If something is overwhelming, it affects you very strongly, and you do not know how to deal with it.

words.ex: The vote was overwhelmingly in favor of the new law.
words.ex_cn: 投票压倒性地支持这项新法律。
words.en: In a way that is very great or very strong; so powerful that you cannot resist it or decide how to react.

words.tr:
n. 化合物；
adj. 复合的；混合的；
words.ex: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
words.ex_cn: 水是由氢和氧组成的化合物。
words.en: A compound is a substance that consists of two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions.

words.tr:
n. 杂交种；混合物；
adj. 混合的；
words.ex: The corn hybrid grows faster than the old type.
words.ex_cn: 这种玉米杂交种比旧品种长得更快。
words.en: A hybrid is a plant or animal that has been produced from two different types of plant or animal, especially to get better characteristics. It can also refer to something that is a mixture of two different things.

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.ex: The benign teacher always helped students after class.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师总是在课后帮助学生。
words.en: A benign substance or process does not have any harmful effects.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.ex: The store is open 24 hours for your convenience.
words.ex_cn: 商店24小时营业，以方便您。
words.en: The state of being able to proceed with something with little effort or difficulty.

words.ex: This store is convenient for buying groceries.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店买杂货很方便。
words.en: If something is convenient, it is easy to use or do, or it is useful and suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The road closure caused an inconvenience to commuters.
words.ex_cn: 道路封闭给通勤者带来了不便。
words.en: Inconvenience refers to the state or quality of being inconvenient; trouble or difficulty caused to one's personal requirements or comfort.

words.ex: The doctor can diagnose the illness quickly.
words.ex_cn: 医生能很快诊断出这种病。
words.en: If someone or something is diagnosed as having a particular illness or problem, their illness or problem is identified. If an illness or problem is diagnosed, it is identified.

words.ex: The doctor made a diagnosis after checking the symptoms.
words.ex_cn: 医生在检查了症状后做出了诊断。
words.en: The identification of the nature of an illness or other problem by examination of the symptoms.

words.ex: The doctor suggested a natural remedy for the cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议了一种治疗感冒的天然疗法。
words.en: A remedy is a cure or a way of making something better.

words.ex: He took a remedial math course to improve his skills.
words.ex_cn: 他上了一门补救数学课程来提高自己的技能。
words.en: Remedial actions or activities are intended to correct something that is wrong or to improve a bad situation.

words.ex: He is receiving therapy for his back pain.
words.ex_cn: 他正在接受治疗以缓解背痛。
words.en: Therapy is the treatment of someone with mental or physical illness without the use of drugs or operations.

words.ex: The therapist helped him feel better after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 治疗专家在事故后帮助他感觉好些了。
words.en: A therapist is a person who is skilled in a particular type of therapy and treats people using it.

words.ex: Walking in the park is therapeutic for her.
words.ex_cn: 在公园散步对她来说有治疗效果。
words.en: having a good effect on the body or mind; contributing to a sense of well-being

words.ex: He went to the clinic for a check-up.
words.ex_cn: 他去诊所做检查。
words.en: A clinic is a place where people receive medical treatment or advice, especially for a particular illness or condition.

words.ex: The doctor gave him a clinical exam.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他做了临床检查。
words.en: Clinical means involving or relating to the direct observation and treatment of patients, rather than theoretical or laboratory studies.

words.tr:
n. 编年史；年代记
v. 按时间顺序记录
words.ex: He writes a chronicle of his daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他记录自己每天的生活。
words.en: A chronicle is a historical account of events arranged in chronological order, typically without analysis or interpretation.

words.ex: He has been chronically ill since childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他从小长期患病。
words.en: In a way that continues for a long time or keeps happening, especially of a disease or problem.

words.tr:
n.  水合物；氢氧化物
v. （使）成水合物
words.ex: The crystal is a hydrate of copper sulfate.
words.ex_cn: 这种晶体是硫酸铜的水合物。
words.en: To hydrate means to cause something to absorb water or to supply water or liquid to someone or something in order to maintain healthy bodily functions. It can also refer to a compound, typically a crystalline one, in which water molecules are chemically bound to another compound or an element.

words.tr: v. 使浸透；使湿透；使满；使饱和
words.ex: The sponge will saturate if you pour too much water.
words.ex_cn: 如果你倒太多水，海绵会吸满。
words.en: To saturate something means to make it completely wet, or to fill it completely with something so that no more can be added.

words.ex: The sponge reached saturation and could not hold more water.
words.ex_cn: 海绵达到饱和，再也吸不下更多水了。
words.en: Saturation is the state or process that occurs when no more of something can be absorbed, combined with, or added.

words.ex: The dog ran through the mud.
words.ex_cn: 狗跑过了泥地。
words.en: Mud is a sticky mixture of earth and water.

words.tr: adj. 泥泞的；模糊不清的；
words.ex: The road became muddy after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，这条路变得泥泞。
words.en: If something is muddy, it is covered in mud or full of mud. If you muddy something, you make it muddy or you make it less clear or more complicated.

words.ex: He washed his hands to remove the dirt.
words.ex_cn: 他洗手以去除污垢。
words.en: Dirt is any substance that makes something unclean, such as mud or dust.

words.ex: The floor is dirty after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 下雨后，地板变得肮脏了。
words.en: If something is dirty, it is marked or covered with stains, spots, or mud, and needs to be cleaned.

words.ex: The workers dug a trench to lay the pipe.
words.ex_cn: 工人们挖了一条沟来铺设管道。
words.en: A trench is a long, narrow ditch. In warfare, trenches are dug by troops to provide shelter from enemy fire.

words.ex: The school needs more resources for students.
words.ex_cn: 学校需要为学生提供更多的资源。
words.en: A resource is a source or supply from which benefit is produced. Typically resources are materials, energy, services, staff, knowledge, or other assets that are transformed to produce benefit and in the process may be consumed or made unavailable.

words.tr: adj. 资源丰富的；机敏的；足智多谋的
words.ex: He is a resourceful man who can fix anything with little material.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个资源丰富的男人，能用很少的材料修好任何东西。
words.en: If someone is resourceful, they are good at finding ways of dealing with problems.

words.ex: We recycle plastic bottles every week.
words.ex_cn: 我们每周回收塑料瓶。
words.en: To recycle means to process used materials so that they can be used again.

words.tr: adj. 可回收利用的；可再循环的；
words.ex: This bottle is recyclable.
words.ex_cn: 这个瓶子是可回收利用的。
words.en: Capable of being recycled; able to be processed and used again.

words.ex: The plastic cup is nonrecyclable.
words.ex_cn: 这个塑料杯是不可回收的。
words.en: Not able to be recycled; not suitable for recycling.

words.tr:
v. 成为三倍；使增至三倍；
n. 三倍的数；三个一组；
adj. 三部分的；
words.ex: The company's profits tripled last year.
words.ex_cn: 该公司去年的利润增长了三倍。
words.en: To triple something means to make it three times as much in size or number.

words.ex: The phone has a silicon chip inside.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机内部有一个硅芯片。
words.en: Silicon is a chemical element with the symbol Si and atomic number 14. It is a hard, brittle crystalline solid with a blue-grey metallic lustre, and is a tetravalent metalloid and semiconductor.

words.tr:
n. 地点；场所；斑点；
v. 发现；识别；
words.ex: This is the spot where we met for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们第一次见面的地方。
words.en: A spot is a particular place or point. It can also refer to a small mark or stain, or a small amount of something. As a verb, it means to see, notice, or recognize someone or something.

words.tr: n. 陶器；制陶手艺；陶器作坊；
words.ex: He makes pottery in his backyard studio.
words.ex_cn: 他在后院的工作室制作陶器。
words.en: Objects such as pots, dishes, and vases that are made out of clay and then baked at high temperatures to make them hard.

words.tr:
n. 潜力；
adj. 潜在的；
words.ex: The young athlete shows great potential.
words.ex_cn: 这位年轻运动员展现出巨大的潜力。
words.en: If you say that someone or something has potential, you mean that they have the necessary abilities or qualities to become successful or useful in the future.

words.ex: The child has great potentiality to learn quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子有很强的学习能力潜力。
words.en: Potentiality refers to the inherent capacity or ability for growth, development, or coming into existence.

words.tr:
n. 聚光灯；
v. 使公众注意；
words.ex: The spotlight shone on the singer during the concert.
words.ex_cn: 演唱会上，聚光灯照在歌手身上。
words.en: A spotlight is a powerful light, for example in a theatre, which can be directed so that it lights up a small area. If someone or something is in the spotlight, they are getting a lot of attention from the public and the media.

words.tr:
n. 预算；预算金额；
adj. 廉价的；花钱少的；
v. 为 ... 做预算；
words.ex: We made a budget for our vacation.
words.ex_cn: 我们为旅行制定了一个预算。
words.en: A budget is a plan that shows how much money a person or organization will earn and how much they will need or be able to spend.

words.ex: The school has a tight budgetary plan.
words.ex_cn: 学校有一个紧张的预算计划。
words.en: Relating to or involving a budget, especially of a government or organization.

words.tr:
n. 目标；对象；
v. 以…为目标；
words.ex: His target is to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的目标是按时完成项目。
words.en: A target is something at which someone is aiming a weapon or other object.

words.tr:
n. 茎；柄；梗
v. 跟踪；偷偷接近；昂首阔步地走
words.ex: The stalk of the sunflower is very tall.
words.ex_cn: 向日葵的茎很高。
words.en: The main stem of a plant, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean. Also, to pursue or approach stealthily.

words.tr:
n. 茎；词干；
v. 起源于(~ from)；
words.ex: The flower grows on a long green stem.
words.ex_cn: 花长在一根长长的绿色茎上。
words.en: The main body or stalk of a plant or shrub, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean; to stop or restrict (the flow of something).

words.ex: The child hurt his limb while playing.
words.ex_cn: 孩子玩耍时伤到了肢体。
words.en: A limb is one of the jointed appendages of an animal used for locomotion or grasping: arm; leg; wing; flipper.

words.ex: The insect flew over the grass.
words.ex_cn: 那只昆虫飞过了草地。
words.en: An insect is a small animal that has six legs. Most insects have wings. Ants, flies, butterflies, and beetles are all insects.

words.ex: The desert has little vegetation.
words.ex_cn: 这个沙漠植被很少。
words.en: Vegetation refers to plants in general, or the plants that are found in a particular area. It can also refer to a life that is dull or inactive, often due to illness or lack of exercise.

words.tr: adj. 无望的；凄凉的；荒凉的；
words.ex: The future looks bleak without a job.
words.ex_cn: 没有工作，未来看起来毫无希望。
words.en: If you describe a situation as bleak, you mean that it seems unlikely to improve or get better.

words.ex: The air feels humid after it rains.
words.ex_cn: 雨后空气感觉湿润。
words.en: You use humid to describe an atmosphere or climate that is very damp, and usually very hot.

words.ex: The humidity in the room made the air feel heavy.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的湿度让空气感觉很闷。
words.en: Humidity is the amount of water vapor in the air. High humidity makes the air feel wet and sticky.

words.tr: adj. 卑微的；谦逊的；虚心的；
words.ex: He lived in a humble house near the river.
words.ex_cn: 他住在河边一座简陋的房子里。
words.en: If you describe someone as humble, you mean that they do not think they are better or more important than other people.

words.tr: adv. 谦恭地；谦卑地；恭恭敬敬地
words.ex: He accepted the award humbly.
words.ex_cn: 他谦逊地接受了奖项。
words.en: In a manner that shows or suggests a modest or low estimate of one's importance; meekly.

words.tr:
v. 跌倒；摔倒；暴跌
n. 摔倒；混乱；暴跌
words.ex: The child tumble down the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 孩子从楼梯上跌倒了。
words.en: If someone or something tumbles, they fall quickly and suddenly, often turning over or spinning as they fall.

words.tr: v. 使屈辱；使丢脸；使蒙羞
words.ex: He tried to humiliate her in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在全班面前羞辱她。
words.en: To humiliate someone means to make them feel ashamed or stupid, especially in front of other people.

words.ex: He felt humiliation after failing the test in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在大家面前考试失败后感到羞辱。
words.en: Humiliation is the embarrassment and shame you feel when someone makes you appear stupid, or when you make a mistake in public.

words.tr: adj. 人道的；仁慈的；人文的
words.ex: The shelter treats animals in a humane way.
words.ex_cn: 这个收容所以人道的方式对待动物。
words.en: If you describe something as humane, you mean that it is good and kind, especially because it decreases suffering.

words.ex: The prison conditions were inhumane.
words.ex_cn: 监狱的条件是不人道的。
words.en: If you describe something as inhumane, you mean that it is extremely cruel.

words.tr: adj. 狂暴的；骚动的；动荡的；汹涌的
words.ex: The turbulent sea made the boat shake.
words.ex_cn: 汹涌的海让船摇晃。
words.en: A turbulent situation, time, or relationship is one in which there is a lot of change, confusion, and often conflict.

words.ex: The political turbulence caused many people to leave the country.
words.ex_cn: 政治骚乱导致许多人离开了这个国家。
words.en: A state of conflict or confusion; irregular atmospheric motion especially when characterized by up-and-down currents.

words.ex: The fierce lion chased the deer.
words.ex_cn: 那只凶猛的狮子追赶着鹿。
words.en: A fierce animal or person is very aggressive or angry.

words.ex: The desert has a harsh climate.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的气候非常严酷。
words.en: If you describe something as harsh, you mean that it is extremely difficult and unpleasant to live in, do, or experience, especially because it is very cold, hot, or violent.

words.ex: The two rooms adjoin each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两个房间彼此相邻。
words.en: If one room, place, or object adjoins another, they are next to each other.

words.tr: adj. 贴邻的；毗连的； v. “adjoin”的现在分词；
words.ex: The two houses are adjoining.
words.ex_cn: 这两所房子是贴邻的。
words.en: Adjoining is used to describe something that is next to or joined with something else.

words.tr:
adj. 联合的；共同的；
n. 关节；接合处；
words.ex: They signed a joint agreement to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一项联合协议来保护环境。
words.en: A joint is a place where two things are joined together, especially the place where two bones are connected in a person's or animal's body.

words.ex: The two houses are adjacent to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两栋房子彼此相邻。
words.en: If one thing is adjacent to another, it is next to it or adjoining it.

words.ex: She adores her little brother.
words.ex_cn: 她非常喜爱她的弟弟。
words.en: If you adore someone, you feel great love and admiration for them.

words.tr: adj. 可爱的；讨人喜欢的
words.ex: The puppy is adorable.
words.ex_cn: 这只小狗很可爱。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is adorable, you are emphasizing that they are very attractive and you feel great affection for them.

words.ex: I admire my teacher for her patience.
words.ex_cn: 我钦佩我的老师有耐心。
words.en: If you admire someone or something, you like and respect them very much.

words.ex: Her courage in facing danger is admirable.
words.ex_cn: 她在面对危险时表现出的勇气令人钦佩。
words.en: If you say that something is admirable, you mean that you approve of it or respect it.

words.tr:
adj. 在前的
adv. 在前面
n. 前头
words.ex: The fore part of the ship is strong.
words.ex_cn: 船的前部很坚固。
words.en: situated or placed in front; the front part of something

words.ex: I cannot foresee what will happen tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我无法预知明天会发生什么。
words.en: If you foresee something, you expect and believe that it will happen.

words.ex: The outcome is foreseeable.
words.ex_cn: 结果是可以预见的。
words.en: If a future event is foreseeable, you know that it will happen or that it can happen, because it is a natural or obvious result of something else that you know.

words.ex: He lost sight of the bird flying away.
words.ex_cn: 他看不见那只飞走的鸟了。
words.en: The ability to see; the act of seeing or the thing seen.

words.tr: n. 先见；预见；先见之明
words.ex: He showed foresight by saving money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他通过为未来存钱展现了远见。
words.en: The ability to predict or the action of predicting what will happen or be needed in the future.

words.ex: We went sightseeing in Paris last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们去巴黎观光了。
words.en: The activity of visiting places of interest in a particular location.

words.ex: His oversight caused the project to fail.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致项目失败。
words.en: An oversight is a mistake that is made by not noticing something or by forgetting to do something.

words.ex: He walked forth to meet the sun.
words.ex_cn: 他向前走去迎接太阳。
words.en: Forward in time, place, or order; onward.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生（或出版等）的；准备好的；
words.ex: The forthcoming book will be released next month.
words.ex_cn: 即将出版的这本书将在下个月发布。
words.en: If something is forthcoming, it is happening or coming soon.

words.tr:
n. 预测；预报；
v. 预测；预报；
words.ex: The weather forecast says it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 天气预测说明天会下雨。
words.en: If you forecast future events, you say what you think is going to happen in the future.

words.tr:
n. 全体演员；
v. 投掷；扔；投射；
words.ex: The cast of the play performed very well.
words.ex_cn: 这部剧的全体演员表演得非常好。
words.en: To cast something means to throw it forcefully in a particular direction.

words.tr:
n. 广播节目；电视节目；
v. 广播；播送；
words.ex: I listened to the morning broadcast on the radio.
words.ex_cn: 我听了早上的广播节目。
words.en: To broadcast is to transmit (a program or some information) by radio or television.

words.tr: n. 广播员；广播公司；节目主持人；电视台
words.ex: The broadcaster announced the news on TV.
words.ex_cn: 广播员在电视上宣布了新闻。
words.en: A broadcaster is a person or organization that transmits programs or information by radio or television.

words.ex: He can foretell the weather by looking at the sky.
words.ex_cn: 他可以通过观察天空来预知天气。
words.en: To tell or indicate beforehand; predict.

words.ex: The horse-drawn carriage was a forerunner of the car.
words.ex_cn: 马车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A forerunner is someone or something that comes before another and is often considered as a sign of what is to follow.

words.tr:
adj. 最重要的；
adv. 首要地；
words.ex: He is the foremost expert in this field.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个领域最重要的专家。
words.en: Most important or prominent; leading.

words.ex: Please tell me beforehand if you can't come.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不能来，请提前告诉我。
words.en: If you do something beforehand, you do it earlier than a particular event.

words.tr: n. 地平线；思想等的范围；眼界；
words.ex: The sun set below the horizon.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在地平线以下落山。
words.en: The horizon is the line at which the earth's surface and the sky appear to meet.

words.ex: The line is horizontal on the graph.
words.ex_cn: 这条线在图上是水平的。
words.en: Parallel to the plane of the horizon; at right angles to the vertical.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.tr: n. 入学介绍；岗前训练；方向；取向；
words.ex: The school held an orientation for new students on Monday.
words.ex_cn: 学校在周一为新生举行了入学介绍。
words.en: The act of orienting or the state of being oriented; the determination of the relative position of something or someone (especially oneself).

words.tr: adj. 东方的（尤指中国和日本）
words.ex: He bought an oriental rug at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一张东方地毯。
words.en: Oriental is used to describe things that come from or are associated with eastern Asia, especially China and Japan.

words.tr: n. 权威；官方机构；权力；权威人士；当局；
words.ex: The teacher is an authority on ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师是古代史方面的权威。
words.en: The power to make decisions or enforce rules.

words.ex: The teacher gave an authoritative answer.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了一个权威性的回答。
words.en: If something is authoritative, it is respected and accepted as true or correct because it comes from a reliable source.

words.ex: The manager will authorize the payment tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 经理明天会批准这笔付款。
words.en: To give official permission for something to happen or to give someone the legal right to do something.

words.ex: The word 'authorization-sation' is not a real English word.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'authorization-sation' 不是真实的英语单词。
words.en: The process of granting official permission or approval.

words.tr:
n. 首都；财富；大写字母；
adj. 大写的；
words.ex: Beijing is the capital of China.
words.ex_cn: 北京是中国的首都。
words.en: The city or town that functions as the seat of government and administrative center of a country or region.

words.tr:
n. 资本家；资本主义者
adj. 资本主义的
words.ex: He is a capitalist who owns a factory.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个拥有工厂的资本家。
words.en: A capitalist is someone who believes in capitalism, an economic system based on private ownership of the means of production and their operation for profit.

words.ex: He believes in capitalism and owns a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他相信资本主义，并拥有一家小企业。
words.en: Capitalism is an economic system in which the means of production are privately owned and operated for profit in a competitive market.

words.ex: The weather bureau issued a storm warning.
words.ex_cn: 气象局发布了风暴预警。
words.en: A bureau is an office, organization, or government department that collects and distributes information.

words.ex: The bureaucrat signed the paper slowly.
words.ex_cn: 这位官僚慢慢地签了那张纸。
words.en: A bureaucrat is an official who works in a bureaucracy, especially one who follows rules and procedures rigidly.

words.tr: adj. 官僚的；官僚主义的；
words.ex: The bureaucratic process made it hard to get a permit.
words.ex_cn: 官僚程序让申请许可证变得困难。
words.en: If you describe a system, organization, or process as bureaucratic, you mean that it is complicated and inefficient because of a large number of rules and procedures.

words.tr: n. 官僚主义；官僚机构
words.ex: He hates the bureaucracy in government offices.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌政府办公室里的官僚主义。
words.en: Bureaucracy refers to a system of government or business that has many complicated rules and ways of doing things.

words.tr:
n. 委员会；佣金；
v. 委托；
words.ex: The commission met to discuss the new law.
words.ex_cn: 委员会开会讨论新法律。
words.en: A commission is a group of people who have been appointed to find out about something or to control something, or the act of doing this. It can also refer to a sum of money that is paid to someone for selling something, which is usually a percentage of the value of the goods sold.

words.ex: The committee meets every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 委员会每周一开会。
words.en: A committee is a group of people who are chosen to do a particular job or make decisions on behalf of a larger group.

words.tr: n. 总部；司令部；指挥部；
words.ex: The company's headquarters is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的总部在纽约。
words.en: The main office or center of control of a company, organization, or military unit.

words.tr: n. 理事会；委员会；议会；
words.ex: The city council made a new rule about recycling.
words.ex_cn: 市政府理事会制定了关于回收的新规定。
words.en: A council is a group of people who are elected to govern a local area such as a city or, in Britain, a county.

words.ex: The councillor spoke at the town meeting.
words.ex_cn: 这位议员在镇会上发表了讲话。
words.en: A councillor is an elected member of a local government council.

words.tr:
n. 研究所；学院；协会；
v. 建立；制定；
words.ex: He works at a research institute.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家研究所工作。
words.en: An institute is an organization set up to do a particular type of work, especially research or teaching. It can also refer to the act of starting something such as a system or an official process.

words.ex: The hospital is a public institution.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院是一家公共机构。
words.en: An institution is a large important organization such as a university, church, or bank.

words.ex: The hospital is an institutional building.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院是一座大型机构的建筑。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of an institution, especially a large organization or public body.

words.tr:
n. 代用品；代替物；
v. 替代；
words.ex: Honey is a good substitute for sugar.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是糖的良好代用品。
words.en: A substitute is something or someone that takes the place or function of another.

words.ex: The substitution of sugar with honey made the cake healthier.
words.ex_cn: 用蜂蜜代替糖使蛋糕更健康。
words.en: The act of replacing one person or thing with another.

words.ex: Five apples constitute a basket.
words.ex_cn: 五个苹果构成一篮子。
words.en: If something constitutes a particular thing, it can be regarded as being that thing.

words.ex: The constitution protects the rights of all citizens.
words.ex_cn: 宪法保护所有公民的权利。
words.en: The constitution of a country or organization is the system of laws which formally states people's rights and duties.

words.ex: He is studying constitutional law at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习宪法。
words.en: Relating to the constitution of a country or organization; in accordance with a political constitution.

words.tr: n. 联邦；共和国；联合体；
words.ex: Australia is a member of the Commonwealth.
words.ex_cn: 澳大利亚是联邦的成员。
words.en: A commonwealth is a traditional English term for a political community founded for the common good. Historically, it has been synonymous with 'republic'.

words.tr:
n. 成分；
adj. 构成的；
words.ex: Sugar is a constituent of soda.
words.ex_cn: 糖是苏打水的一种成分。
words.en: A constituent is a part of a whole. In politics, a constituent is a person who is represented by an elected official.

words.ex: The politician lost his constituency after the scandal.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客在丑闻后失去了他的支持者。
words.en: A constituency is a group of people in a country or area who are entitled to vote in an election, or the area itself.

words.ex: The case will be heard in court next week.
words.ex_cn: 这个案件将于下周在法院审理。
words.en: A court is a place where legal matters are decided by a judge and jury or by a magistrate.

words.ex: He showed courtesy by holding the door open.
words.ex_cn: 他为别人扶着门，表现得很礼貌。
words.en: Courtesy is polite behavior, or a polite action or remark.

words.ex: He was courteous to everyone he met.
words.ex_cn: 他对遇到的每个人都很有礼貌。
words.en: Someone who is courteous is polite and respectful to other people.

words.tr: adj. 联邦的；联邦制的；联邦政府的；
words.ex: The federal government passed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 联邦政府通过了一项新法律。
words.en: A federal system of government is one in which there is a central government and separate governments for each of the states or regions.

words.ex: The countries formed a federation to share resources.
words.ex_cn: 这些国家组成了一个联盟来共享资源。
words.en: A federation is a group of states or organizations that have joined together to form a single entity with a central government or authority.

words.ex: The minister signed the new law.
words.ex_cn: 部长签署了新法律。
words.en: A minister is a person who is in charge of a particular government department or a member of the clergy in some Christian churches.

words.ex: The ministerial meeting will be held tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 部长会议将在明天举行。
words.en: Relating to a minister or ministry, especially in government or the church.

words.tr: v. 给予（药物或治疗）；管理；实施；
words.ex: The nurse will administer the medicine to the patient.
words.ex_cn: 护士会给病人服药。
words.en: To administer means to manage or oversee the execution, use, or conduct of something; to dispense or apply (a remedy or drug).

words.ex: The administrative office handles school records.
words.ex_cn: 行政办公室负责管理学校档案。
words.en: Relating to the management of a company, organization, or institution.

words.ex: The administration of the school is very organized.
words.ex_cn: 学校的行政管理非常有条理。
words.en: The process or activity of running a business, organization, etc., or the people who run it.

words.ex: The ministry of education controls schools.
words.ex_cn: 教育部管理学校。
words.en: A ministry is a government department, especially in Britain, which is responsible for a particular area of administration, such as health or education.

words.ex: He hired a legal lawyer to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他请了一位法律律师来帮助他。
words.en: Relating to the law or to lawyers, or permitted or required by law.

words.tr: v. 使合法化；使得到法律认可
words.ex: The country plans to legalize marijuana next year.
words.ex_cn: 该国计划明年将大麻合法化。
words.en: To make something legal or acceptable according to the law.

words.ex: The legalization of marijuana is happening in some states.
words.ex_cn: 大麻的合法化正在一些州发生。
words.en: The act of making something legal that was previously illegal.

words.tr: v. 制定法律；用立法规定
words.ex: The government will legislate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将制定新规则。
words.en: To legislate means to make or enact laws.

words.ex: The new legislation bans plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法规禁止使用塑料袋。
words.en: Legislation refers to the process of making or enacting laws by a government or other authority.

words.ex: The legislator voted for a new law.
words.ex_cn: 这位立法者投票支持了一项新法律。
words.en: A legislator is a person who is a member of a legislature, especially in a democratic country.

words.tr: adj. 立法的；制定法律的；
words.ex: The legislative branch makes laws.
words.ex_cn: 立法部门制定法律。
words.en: Relating to the making of laws.

words.ex: The parliament passed a new law about education.
words.ex_cn: 国会通过了一项关于教育的新法律。
words.en: A parliament is a legislative body of government, typically composed of elected representatives, that is responsible for making laws and representing the interests of the people.

words.ex: The parliamentary debate lasted all night.
words.ex_cn: 议会辩论持续了一整夜。
words.en: Relating to, enacted by, or suitable for a parliament.

words.ex: The virus can propagate quickly among people.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒可以在人群中迅速传播。
words.en: To propagate something means to spread it and encourage more people to believe in it or support it.

words.ex: The propagation of the rumor spread quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个谣言的传播很快。
words.en: The act of spreading something, especially information or ideas, or the process by which plants or animals produce more of their own kind.

words.ex: The government used propaganda to influence people's opinions.
words.ex_cn: 政府使用宣传来影响人们的观点。
words.en: Information, especially of a biased or misleading nature, used to promote a political cause or point of view.

words.tr: v. 公开宣传（英式拼写变体）
words.ex: The word 'publicize-ise' is not a real word.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'publicize-ise' 不是真实存在的词。
words.en: To make something widely known, especially through the media.

words.tr:
adj. 公众的；
n. 公众；公共场所；
words.ex: The park is open to the public.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园对公众开放。
words.en: Relating to or involving people in general, rather than being limited to a particular group of people.

words.ex: He publicly apologized for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他公开为自己的错误道歉。
words.en: In a way that is open or visible to the public; not privately.

words.ex: The company got a lot of publicity from the TV ad.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司从电视广告中获得了大量宣传。
words.en: Publicity is the activity of making sure that someone or something attracts a lot of interest or attention from the public, especially by providing information about them in newspapers, on television, etc.

words.ex: He donate money to the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他向贫困儿童捐赠钱。
words.en: To donate means to give something, especially money, to a person or organization that needs help.

words.ex: The donor gave money to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 捐赠者向医院捐了钱。
words.en: A donor is a person or organization that gives something, especially money, to a charity or other organization.

words.ex: The hospital received a donation of books.
words.ex_cn: 医院收到了一批书籍捐赠。
words.en: A donation is a gift which is given to a charity or other organization.

words.ex: He endow a library with books.
words.ex_cn: 他捐赠了一图书馆的书。
words.en: If someone is endowed with a particular quality or ability, they naturally have it.

words.ex: The university received a large endowment from a philanthropist.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学收到了一位慈善家的大量捐赠。
words.en: An endowment is a gift of money that is made to an institution or community in order to provide it with an annual income.

words.ex: The charity helps poor children get food and education.
words.ex_cn: 这个慈善团体帮助贫困儿童获得食物和教育。
words.en: An organization that helps people in need, or the act of giving money, food, or help to those who need it.

words.tr: adj. 仁慈的；慈善事业的；
words.ex: She gave charitable donations to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 她向穷人捐赠了仁慈的善款。
words.en: A charitable organization or activity helps and supports people who are ill, very poor, or who have disabilities.

words.tr: v. 贡献；促成；捐献；投稿；
words.ex: He contributes money to the charity.
words.ex_cn: 他向慈善机构捐款。
words.en: If you contribute to something, you help to cause it or make it happen.

words.ex: His contribution helped the team win.
words.ex_cn: 他的贡献帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: A contribution is a gift or payment to a common fund or collection, or the part played by a person or thing in bringing about a result or helping something to advance.

words.tr: n. 投稿人；贡献者；因素；
words.ex: He is a contributor to the local newspaper.
words.ex_cn: 他是当地报纸的投稿人。
words.en: A contributor is someone who gives something, such as money, time, or ideas, to help achieve or provide something.

words.ex: The village sent a tribute of grain to the king.
words.ex_cn: 村庄向国王进贡了谷物。
words.en: A tribute is something that you say, do, or make to show your admiration and respect for someone.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.ex: The accident is attributable to poor road conditions.
words.ex_cn: 这起事故可归因于糟糕的路况。
words.en: Capable of being attributed to someone or something.

words.ex: The teacher will distribute the books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将把书分发给学生。
words.en: If you distribute things, you hand them or deliver them to a number of people.

words.ex: The distributor delivers snacks to local stores.
words.ex_cn: 这家经销商将零食配送到本地商店。
words.en: A distributor is a company or person that supplies goods to shops or other businesses, or a device that sends out electricity to the spark plugs in an engine.

words.ex: The distributive property says 3 times (4 + 5) equals 3 times 4 plus 3 times 5.
words.ex_cn: 分配律说 3 乘以 (4 + 5) 等于 3 乘以 4 加上 3 乘以 5。
words.en: Relating to the way that something is shared out among a group or spread over an area.

words.ex: The distribution of students in the class is even.
words.ex_cn: 班级里学生的分布是均匀的。
words.en: The process of giving out or spreading something, or the way in which something is spread or arranged over an area or among a group of people.

words.tr: v. 重新分配；再分配；重分配；
words.ex: The government will redistribute the money to poor families.
words.ex_cn: 政府将把钱重新分配给贫困家庭。
words.en: To redistribute something means to distribute it in a different way, so that it is shared more fairly or equally.

words.ex: The government plans redistribution of wealth to help the poor.
words.ex_cn: 政府计划重新分配财富以帮助穷人。
words.en: The act of distributing something again or differently, especially wealth or resources.

words.ex: The new regime changed the tax laws.
words.ex_cn: 新的管理制度改变了税法。
words.en: A regime is the set of rules or the way that a country or organization is governed, especially when it is considered to be strict or unfair.

words.ex: The queen's reign lasted 70 years.
words.ex_cn: 女王的统治持续了70年。
words.en: The period during which a sovereign rules; to hold royal office; to prevail

words.ex: Exercise can reinforce your muscles.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的肌肉。
words.en: To reinforce something means to make it stronger or more effective.

words.ex: The teacher gave candy as a reinforcement for good behavior.
words.ex_cn: 老师用糖果作为良好行为的强化物。
words.en: Reinforcement is the process of encouraging or establishing a belief or pattern of behavior, especially by encouragement or reward.

words.ex: Exercise can enhance your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提高你的健康。
words.en: To enhance something means to improve its value, quality, or attractiveness.

words.tr:
n. 发展；进步；提前；
adj. 预先的；在前的；
v. 前进；发展；提前；
words.ex: The advance of technology has changed our lives.
words.ex_cn: 科技的发展改变了我们的生活。
words.en: If you advance a cause, interest, or claim, you support it and help it to succeed.

words.tr: adj. 先进的；高级的； v. 提前；前进；“advance”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This school uses advanced technology in classrooms.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校在教室里使用先进的技术。
words.en: An advanced system, method, or design is modern and has been developed from an earlier version of the same thing.

words.ex: The advancement of technology helps people live better.
words.ex_cn: 技术的进步帮助人们生活得更好。
words.en: The process of promoting a cause or plan; the act of moving forward or making progress.

words.ex: He is loyal to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友忠诚。
words.en: Someone who is loyal remains firm in their friendship or support for a person or thing.

words.ex: His loyalty to his friends never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的忠诚从未改变。
words.en: The quality of being loyal to someone or something.

words.ex: The royal family lives in a big palace.
words.ex_cn: 皇室住在一座大宫殿里。
words.en: Royal is used to describe something that is connected with a king, queen, or emperor, or with their family. It can also describe something that is splendid or magnificent, befitting a king or queen.

words.ex: The royalty lived in a large palace.
words.ex_cn: 皇族住在一座大宫殿里。
words.en: Royalty refers to people of royal blood or status, or a sum of money paid to an author, composer, etc., for each copy of a work sold or for each public performance of their work.

words.tr:
n. 敬礼；致敬；行礼
v. 敬礼；致敬；行礼
words.ex: The soldier gave a salute to the officer.
words.ex_cn: 士兵向军官敬礼。
words.en: If you salute someone, you greet them or show your respect with a formal sign. Soldiers usually salute officers by raising their right hand so that their fingers touch their forehead.

words.ex: He wrote a warm salutation at the start of the letter.
words.ex_cn: 他在信的开头写了一个热情的问候语。
words.en: A salutation is a greeting or an expression of goodwill.

words.tr:
n. 最高统治者；君主；元首
adj. 独立自主的；拥有最高统治权的
words.ex: The sovereign makes important decisions for the country.
words.ex_cn: 君主为国家做出重要决定。
words.en: A sovereign is a king, queen, or other supreme ruler.

words.ex: The country values its sovereignty.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家重视它的主权。
words.en: Sovereignty is the power that a country has to govern itself or another country or state.

words.tr:
n. 状态；州；国家；
v. 陈述；说明；
adj. 国事礼仪（或规格）的；州的；
words.ex: The state of the car is very poor.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的状态非常差。
words.en: A state is a condition or way of being that something or someone is in. It can also refer to a nation or territory considered as an organized political community under one government.

words.ex: The company made a statement about the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 公司就新政策发布了一项声明。
words.en: A statement is something that you say or write which gives information in a formal or definite way.

words.ex: The emperor ruled the country for many years.
words.ex_cn: 这位皇帝统治这个国家很多年。
words.en: A male sovereign ruler of an empire.

words.ex: The empress ruled the empire with wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 皇后以智慧统治帝国。
words.en: A woman who is the sovereign ruler of an empire or the wife of an emperor.

words.ex: The imperial palace was built long ago.
words.ex_cn: 这座帝国宫殿是很久以前建造的。
words.en: relating to an empire or an emperor; majestic or superior in quality or size

words.ex: The country practiced imperialism in the 1800s.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在19世纪实行帝国主义。
words.en: Imperialism is a policy or ideology of extending a country's rule over foreign nations, often by military force or by gaining political and economic control of other areas.

words.tr:
n. 帝国主义者
adj. 帝国主义的
words.ex: The imperialist country took over many colonies.
words.ex_cn: 这个帝国主义国家占领了许多殖民地。
words.en: An imperialist is a person who supports or practices imperialism, which is a policy of extending a country's power and influence through colonization, use of military force, or other means.

words.ex: He finally admit his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, you agree, often unwillingly, that it is true.

words.ex: The ticket is your admission to the concert.
words.ex_cn: 这张票是进入音乐会的许可。
words.en: An admission is a statement in which you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, or the act of allowing someone to enter a place or organization.

words.ex: He was denied admittance to the concert.
words.ex_cn: 他被拒绝进入音乐会。
words.en: Permission to enter a place.

words.tr: adv. 公认地；普遍承认地；诚然；
words.ex: Admittedly, he is not the best player, but he works hard.
words.ex_cn: 公认地，他不是最好的球员，但他很努力。
words.en: Used to express that you accept something is true or that you agree with it, even though you may not like it.

words.tr:
n. 许可证；
v. 允许；准许；
words.ex: He showed his fishing permit to the officer.
words.ex_cn: 他向官员出示了他的钓鱼许可证。
words.en: If someone permits something, they allow it to happen. If they permit you to do something, they allow you to do it.

words.ex: He asked for permission to leave early.
words.ex_cn: 他请求允许早点离开。
words.en: If someone who has authority over you gives you permission to do something, they say that they will allow you to do it.

words.tr: adj. 可容许的；可承认的
words.ex: It is permissible to use a calculator in this test.
words.ex_cn: 在这次考试中使用计算器是允许的。
words.en: If something is permissible, it is considered to be acceptable because it does not break any laws or rules.

words.tr: adj. 放任的；纵容的；许可的
words.ex: Her parents are permissive and let her stay out late.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母很宽容，让她很晚才回家。
words.en: A permissive person, society, or system allows people a lot of freedom to do what they want.

words.ex: The radio transmits music to listeners.
words.ex_cn: 收音机将音乐传递给听众。
words.en: To send or pass something from one person, place, or thing to another.

words.tr: n. 传播者；发射机；送话机
words.ex: The radio transmitter sends signals to the receiver.
words.ex_cn: 无线电发射器将信号发送给接收器。
words.en: A transmitter is a device that sends out signals in the form of radio waves, or someone who sends or passes on something.

words.ex: The signal transmission is clear and strong.
words.ex_cn: 信号传输清晰而强劲。
words.en: The act or process of sending or passing something from one place, person, or thing to another.

words.ex: The freight train carried boxes to the city.
words.ex_cn: 货运列车把箱子运到了城市。
words.en: Freight refers to goods transported in bulk by truck, train, ship, or aircraft. It can also mean the charge for such transportation.

words.ex: He will submit his homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会提交他的作业。
words.en: To yield or surrender (oneself) to the will or authority of another.

words.ex: His submission to the boss ended the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他对老板的屈服结束了这场冲突。
words.en: The act of submitting something to someone for their decision or consideration; the state of being submissive or obedient.

words.tr: adj. 顺从的；服从的；恭顺的；
words.ex: The submissive dog waited quietly for its owner's command.
words.ex_cn: 这只顺从的狗安静地等待主人的命令。
words.en: If you are submissive, you obey someone without arguing.

words.ex: The climbers reached the summit of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 登山者到达了山顶。
words.en: The highest point of a hill or mountain; a meeting between heads of government.

words.ex: The climax of the movie was a big chase scene.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的高潮是一场大追捕场景。
words.en: The climax is the most exciting or important part of a play, film, or piece of music, which usually happens near the end.

words.tr:
n. 高峰；顶峰；
v. 达到高峰；达到最高值；
words.ex: The mountain peak is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 这座山的高峰被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or level of something; the pointed top of a mountain.

words.ex: The lamp emits a soft light.
words.ex_cn: 灯发出柔和的光。
words.en: To emit means to send out something such as light, heat, sound, gas, etc.

words.ex: The factory reduces emission to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 工厂减少排放以保护环境。
words.en: An emission is the production and discharge of something, especially gas or radiation.

words.ex: The emitter sends out light.
words.ex_cn: 发射器发出光。
words.en: An entity, such as a factory or vehicle, that releases something, typically greenhouse gases, into the atmosphere.

words.ex: He omitted the last word in the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他省略了句子中的最后一个词。
words.en: If you omit something, you do not include it in an activity or piece of work, deliberately or accidentally.

words.ex: The omission of his name was an accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的名字被漏掉是无意的。
words.en: An omission is something that has not been included or has not been done, either deliberately or accidentally.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；间歇的
words.ex: The rain is intermittent today.
words.ex_cn: 今天雨断断续续地下。
words.en: Something that is intermittent happens occasionally rather than continuously.

words.tr: v. 承诺；犯（罪、错）；（公开地）表达意见；
words.ex: He commit to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺帮助他的朋友。
words.en: To commit means to carry out or perpetrate a mistake, crime, or immoral act; or to pledge or bind oneself to a certain course of action.

words.ex: He made a commitment to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺按时完成这个项目。
words.en: A commitment is something that regularly takes up some of your time because of an agreement you have made or because of responsibilities that you have.

words.tr:
n. 辩论；讨论；
v. 辩论；讨论；
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: If you maintain something, you continue to have it, and do not let it stop or grow weaker.

words.ex: The cost of maintenance is low for this car.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的维持费用很低。
words.en: The process of preserving a condition or situation or the state of being preserved.

words.ex: He retains his old photos in a box.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧照片保存在一个盒子里。
words.en: If you retain something, you keep it or continue to have it.

words.ex: The company improved data retention after upgrading its system.
words.ex_cn: 公司在升级系统后提高了数据保留能力。
words.en: The action of retaining something; the continued possession, use, or control of something.

words.ex: The police will detain the suspect for questioning.
words.ex_cn: 警察将扣留嫌疑人进行审问。
words.en: If someone is detained, they are officially held in a place, especially a prison, and are not allowed to leave.

words.ex: The student was sent to detention for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这名学生因违反规则被留校滞留。
words.en: Detention is the act of detaining someone or the state of being detained in official custody, especially as a political prisoner.

words.ex: The farmer works hard to sustain his crops.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民努力维持他的庄稼。
words.en: To sustain something means to continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

words.ex: We need sustainable energy to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要可持续的能源来保护环境。
words.en: If something is sustainable, it can be maintained or continued at a certain rate or level without causing damage or depletion of resources.

words.ex: The city plans for sustainability by using solar energy.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市通过使用太阳能来实现可持续性。
words.en: Sustainability is the ability to maintain or support a process continuously over time. In the context of environmental science, it refers to the avoidance of the depletion of natural resources in order to maintain an ecological balance.

words.ex: This rule pertains to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If one thing pertains to another, it relates, belongs, or applies to it.

words.ex: He worked hard to attain his goals.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以达到他的目标。
words.en: If you attain something, you gain it or achieve it, often after a lot of effort.

words.ex: His attainment of the goal took many years.
words.ex_cn: 他达到这个目标花了多年时间。
words.en: The act of achieving something, especially through effort; a skill or accomplishment that has been achieved.

words.ex: The clown entertains the children with funny tricks.
words.ex_cn: 小丑用滑稽的把戏娱乐孩子们。
words.en: To entertain someone means to amuse or interest them, for example by telling them stories or jokes, or by playing music for them.

words.ex: Watching movies is a popular entertainment.
words.ex_cn: 看电影是一种流行的休闲娱乐。
words.en: Entertainment refers to performances or activities that are intended to amuse or interest an audience.

words.tr: adj. 有趣的；使人愉快的； v. 款待；“entertain”的现在分词；
words.ex: The clown gave an entertaining show.
words.ex_cn: 小丑表演了一场有趣的节目。
words.en: Providing amusement or enjoyment.

words.ex: The country has an underdeveloped economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家经济不发达。
words.en: An underdeveloped country or region is one that is less developed economically and socially than most others, with many of its people living in poverty.

words.ex: He offended the law by stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他偷窃触犯了法律。
words.en: If you offend someone, you upset or embarrass them by saying or doing something that they think is rude or insulting.

words.tr: n. 犯罪；冒犯；进攻；控方
words.ex: The offense-ce led to his arrest.
words.ex_cn: 这个犯罪行为导致他被逮捕。
words.en: A misspelling of 'offense', meaning a breach of law or rule; a feeling of hurt or resentment.

words.tr: n. 得罪人的人；犯罪者；违法者；
words.ex: He was punished because he was an offender who hurt his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他因为是一个得罪朋友的人而受到惩罚。
words.en: An offender is a person who commits a crime or does something wrong.

words.tr: adj. 冒犯的；令人不快的；进攻性的；
words.ex: His offensive words made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 他冒犯的话让她哭了。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as offensive, you mean that it is rude or insulting.

words.ex: He does not want to intrude on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他不想插话他们的谈话。
words.en: To intrude means to enter somewhere or become involved in a situation where you are not wanted or are not supposed to be.

words.ex: The intrusion of strangers made her feel unsafe.
words.ex_cn: 陌生人的闯入让她感到不安全。
words.en: An intrusion is an unwanted event or person in a situation where they are not welcome or do not belong.

words.ex: The intruder broke into the house at night.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者在晚上闯入了房子。
words.en: An intruder is a person who enters a place or situation where they are not wanted.

words.ex: The army tried to invade the neighboring country.
words.ex_cn: 军队试图侵犯邻国。
words.en: To enter a country, town, or region by force in order to take control of it.

words.ex: The invasion of privacy is a serious problem.
words.ex_cn: 侵犯隐私是一个严重的问题。
words.en: An invasion is an instance of invading a country or region with an armed force.

words.ex: The invader came from a faraway land.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者来自一个遥远的地方。
words.en: An invader is someone who enters a place by force in order to conquer or occupy it.

words.ex: The invasive plant spreads quickly and kills other plants.
words.ex_cn: 这种侵入性植物生长迅速，会杀死其他植物。
words.en: If you describe something as invasive, you mean that it spreads very quickly and is difficult to stop.

words.ex: The soldiers defend their country from enemies.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们保卫自己的国家免受敌人入侵。
words.en: To defend means to protect someone or something from attack, harm, or criticism. It can also involve arguing in support of someone or something.

words.ex: The team's defence was very strong in the match.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在比赛中防守非常坚强。
words.en: The action of defending from or resisting attack.

words.ex: He took a defensive position to protect the goal.
words.ex_cn: 他采取了防守姿势来保护球门。
words.en: If someone is defensive, they are behaving in a way that shows they are anxious or angry because they feel that they are being criticized.

words.tr: n. 防御者；防守队员；拥护者；卫冕者
words.ex: The defender stopped the ball with his foot.
words.ex_cn: 防守球员用脚挡住了球。
words.en: A defender is someone who defends a place or person, or who supports an idea or policy.

words.ex: The defendant spoke calmly in court.
words.ex_cn: 被告在法庭上平静地发言。
words.en: A defendant is a person or entity against whom a criminal or civil action is brought in a court of law.

words.ex: He used a pretext to leave the meeting early.
words.ex_cn: 他找了个借口提前离开了会议。
words.en: A pretext is a false reason that you give for doing something, usually something bad, in order to hide the real reason.

words.tr:
v. 抗议；
n. 抗议活动；
words.ex: The students protest against the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 学生们抗议新的校规。
words.en: A protest is the act of saying or showing publicly that you object to something.

words.ex: He won the spelling contest.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了拼写比赛。
words.en: A contest is a competition or a struggle for victory between individuals or groups.

words.ex: The contestant won the singing competition.
words.ex_cn: 这位竞争者赢得了歌唱比赛。
words.en: A contestant is someone who takes part in a competition or contest.

words.ex: His rude words provoked her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了她。
words.en: If you provoke someone, you deliberately annoy them and try to make them behave aggressively.

words.ex: His rude comment was a provocation to start a fight.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的评论是一种挑衅，想引发争斗。
words.en: If you describe someone's action as a provocation, you mean that it is likely to cause a reaction or argument, especially a violent or angry one.

words.ex: His provocative words made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 他挑衅的话让所有人都生气了。
words.en: If you describe something as provocative, you mean that it is intended to make people react angrily or argue against it.

words.ex: The song evokes happy memories of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌唤起了对童年的美好回忆。
words.en: To evoke a particular memory, idea, emotion, or response means to cause it to occur.

words.ex: Farmers irrigate their fields with water from the river.
words.ex_cn: 农民用河里的水灌溉他们的田地。
words.en: To supply land or crops with water by means of channels or pipes.

words.ex: Farmers use irrigation to water their crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民使用灌溉来浇灌庄稼。
words.en: Irrigation is the process of supplying water to land or crops to help growth, typically by means of channels.

words.ex: He is irritable when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候容易烦躁。
words.en: If someone is irritable, they are easily annoyed.

words.tr: v. 激怒；使急躁；使疼痛
words.ex: Loud noises irritate my baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音会激怒我的宝宝。
words.en: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

words.ex: The irritation on his arm hurt when he touched it.
words.ex_cn: 他手臂上的疼痛处一碰就疼。
words.en: Irritation is the feeling of annoyance, especially when something keeps happening that you do not like.

words.tr: adj. 惹人生气的； v. “irritate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The loud noise is irritating.
words.ex_cn: 这噪音很惹人生气。
words.en: If you describe something as irritating, you mean that it keeps annoying you.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.ex: He will inevitably fail if he doesn't study.
words.ex_cn: 如果他不学习，他不可避免地会失败。
words.en: If something will inevitably happen, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.ex: The fence safeguards the garden from animals.
words.ex_cn: 围栏保护花园免受动物侵扰。
words.en: A safeguard is a measure taken to protect someone or something from potential harm or danger.

words.tr:
n. 保卫；警卫；
v. 守卫；
words.ex: The guard stands at the gate to protect the building.
words.ex_cn: 保卫人员站在门口保护大楼。
words.en: A guard is a person who protects a place, person, or thing, or who prevents people from escaping from a place.

words.ex: The old man is the guardian of his grandchildren.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人是他的孙子孙女的保护人。
words.en: A guardian is someone who has the legal authority and responsibility to take care of someone else, especially a child whose parents have died.

words.tr:
v. （使）获得；
adj. 安全的；稳定的；
words.ex: He worked hard to secure a job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以获得一份工作。
words.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

words.tr: n. 安全；保障；防护措施；
words.ex: The school improved security to protect students.
words.ex_cn: 学校加强了安全措施以保护学生。
words.en: Security refers to the state of being free from danger or threat, or measures taken to ensure safety.

words.ex: He missed three consecutive days of school.
words.ex_cn: 他连续三天没上学。
words.en: Consecutive events, numbers, etc. follow one after another without an interruption.

words.ex: The knight held up his shield to block the arrow.
words.ex_cn: 骑士举起盾牌来挡箭。
words.en: A shield is a piece of armor held in the hand or worn on the arm to protect the body from missiles or blows. It can also refer to something that protects or defends someone or something from harm or danger.

words.tr: v. 使遭危险或伤害；危害；危及
words.ex: Pollution can endanger animals.
words.ex_cn: 污染会危及动物。
words.en: To put someone or something at risk or in danger.

words.tr: adj. 濒临灭绝的；有灭绝危险的； v. “endanger”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The panda is an endangered animal.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫是一种濒临灭绝的动物。
words.en: An animal or plant that is endangered is in danger of becoming extinct.

words.ex: The broken glass is a hazard.
words.ex_cn: 碎玻璃是危险。
words.en: A hazard is something which could be dangerous to you, your health or safety, or your plans or reputation.

words.ex: The chemicals are hazardous to health.
words.ex_cn: 这些化学物质对健康有危险。
words.en: Something that is hazardous is dangerous, especially to people's health or safety.

words.ex: He bought a stake in the new company.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了这家新公司的股份。
words.en: A stake is a pointed stick or post that is pushed into the ground, for example to support a young tree. It can also refer to a share or interest in a business, situation, or system.

words.ex: He put his job in jeopardy by being late every day.
words.ex_cn: 他因为每天迟到而危及了自己的工作。
words.en: Jeopardy is a situation of exposure to danger or harm.

words.tr: v. 危及；使处于危险中
words.ex: Don't jeopardize your future by skipping class.
words.ex_cn: 不要因为逃课而危及你的未来。
words.en: An archaic or dialectal variant of 'jeopardize' or 'jeopardise'.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.ex: He went on an adventure in the jungle.
words.ex_cn: 他去丛林里冒险。
words.en: An adventure is an exciting experience or undertaking that is typically bold, sometimes risky.

words.ex: The adventurer climbed the high mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 这位冒险家独自爬上了高山。
words.en: An adventurer is someone who enjoys or seeks adventure, especially someone who travels to unknown or dangerous places.

words.tr: adj. 有冒险精神的；敢于创新的；
words.ex: He is an adventurous boy who loves climbing mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢爬山的有冒险精神的男孩。
words.en: Willing to take risks or to try out new methods, ideas, or experiences.

words.ex: The advent of smartphones changed how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的到来改变了我们的交流方式。
words.en: The arrival of a notable person, thing, or event.

words.ex: The hikers faced great peril in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者在风暴中面临巨大危险。
words.en: Peril refers to serious and immediate danger.

words.ex: The climb was perilous in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 在暴风雨中，这次攀登非常危险。
words.en: Full of danger or risk.

words.ex: He lost his fortune in the stock market.
words.ex_cn: 他在股市中失去了他的财产。
words.en: A large amount of money or assets; chance or luck as an external force in human affairs.

words.ex: He is fortunate to have a good job.
words.ex_cn: 他很幸运拥有一份好工作。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is fortunate, you mean that they are lucky.

words.ex: He lost his job, which was a great misfortune.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了工作，这是一场巨大的不幸。
words.en: An unfortunate condition or event.

words.ex: The savage wolf howled under the moon.
words.ex_cn: 那头野性的狼在月光下嚎叫。
words.en: A savage person or animal is very fierce and violent.

words.ex: He surpassed his brother in math scores.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学成绩上超过了他弟弟。
words.en: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.tr:
v. （使）纠缠；使陷入；使混乱
n. 纠缠；混乱；纠纷
words.ex: The cat got into a tangle with the yarn.
words.ex_cn: 猫和毛线缠在一起了。
words.en: If something is tangled or tangles, it becomes twisted together in an untidy way.

words.tr: adj. 缠结的； v. “tangle”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The hair was tangled after the wind.
words.ex_cn: 头发被风吹得打结了。
words.en: If something is tangled, it is twisted together untidily and is difficult to unravel or separate.

words.tr:
n. 脏乱；杂乱；
v. 弄糟；
words.ex: The room was a mess after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对后房间一片狼藉。
words.en: A mess is a situation that is confused and full of problems, or something that is dirty or untidy.

words.ex: His room is messy with clothes everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 他的房间很杂乱，衣服到处都是。
words.en: If you describe something as messy, you mean that it is untidy or dirty.

words.ex: The room was in chaos after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对之后，房间一片混乱。
words.en: A state of complete disorder and confusion.

words.ex: The room was chaotic after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对后房间一片混乱。
words.en: If a situation, place, or system is chaotic, it is in a state of complete disorder and confusion.

words.tr: n. 令人讨厌的或繁重的工作；
words.ex: Washing dishes is a boring chore.
words.ex_cn: 洗碗是一件烦人的琐事。
words.en: A chore is a task or piece of work that is often boring or unpleasant but needs to be done regularly.

words.ex: The room was in complete disorder.
words.ex_cn: 房间一片混乱。
words.en: A disorder is a state of confusion or untidiness, or a medical problem that affects the mind or body.

words.ex: He filled the tank with water.
words.ex_cn: 他把罐子装满了水。
words.en: A tank is a large container for holding liquid or gas, or a heavily armored fighting vehicle carrying guns and moving on a continuous articulated metal track.

words.tr:
n. 攻击；袭击；
v. 攻击；袭击；
words.ex: The attack happened at night.
words.ex_cn: 这次攻击发生在夜晚。
words.en: To attack means to try to hurt or defeat someone or something by using force or violence.

words.ex: The movie caused a feeling of terror in the audience.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影让观众感到恐怖。
words.en: Terror is a very strong feeling of fear, especially fear that you experience suddenly.

words.tr: n. 恐怖主义；恐怖行动
words.ex: The country is fighting terrorism with strong laws.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家通过严格的法律打击恐怖主义。
words.en: Terrorism is the use of violence and intimidation in the pursuit of political aims.

words.ex: The police caught the terrorist near the station.
words.ex_cn: 警察在车站附近抓住了这名恐怖分子。
words.en: A terrorist is a person who uses violent and intimidating methods in the pursuit of political aims.

words.ex: The loud thunder terrified the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的雷声吓坏了那个孩子。
words.en: If something terrifies you, it makes you feel extremely frightened.

words.tr: adj. 令人害怕的；令人恐惧的； v. “terrify”的现在分词；
words.ex: The dark forest looked terrifying at night.
words.ex_cn: 那个黑暗的森林在晚上看起来令人害怕。
words.en: If you describe something as terrifying, you mean that it makes you feel extremely frightened.

words.tr: adj. 恐惧的；受惊吓的； v. “terrify”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The child was terrified of the dark.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子害怕黑暗。
words.en: If you are terrified, you are extremely frightened.

words.tr: adj. 可怕的；极坏的；糟糕的；
words.ex: The storm caused a terrible flood.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴引发了一场可怕的洪水。
words.en: If something is terrible, it is very bad or of very poor quality.

words.ex: I am terribly sorry for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 我为这个错误非常抱歉。
words.en: Used to emphasize the extreme degree of something.

words.ex: The loud noise frightened the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音吓到了孩子。
words.en: If something or someone frightens you, they cause you to suddenly feel afraid, anxious, or nervous.

words.ex: The loud noise gave her a sudden fright.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让她吓了一跳。
words.en: A sudden intense feeling of fear.

words.tr: adj. 惊吓的；受惊的；害怕的； v. “frighten”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The child was frightened by the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 孩子被巨大的噪音吓到了。
words.en: If you are frightened, you are anxious or afraid, often because of something that has just happened or that you think may happen.

words.tr: adj. 引起恐惧的；使惊恐的；骇人的； v. “frighten”的现在分词；
words.ex: The dark forest looked frightening at night.
words.ex_cn: 那个黑暗的森林在晚上看起来很吓人。
words.en: If you say that something is frightening, you mean that it makes you feel afraid or anxious.

words.tr:
n. 恐慌；
v. 感到恐慌；
words.ex: A panic spread through the crowd when the fire alarm rang.
words.ex_cn: 当火警响起时，人群陷入了恐慌。
words.en: Panic is a very strong feeling of anxiety or fear, which makes you act without thinking carefully.

words.ex: The disease afflicted many people in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病使村子里许多人遭受痛苦。
words.en: If you are afflicted by pain, illness, or misfortune, it causes you great suffering and distress.

words.ex: He screamed in agony after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒后痛苦地大叫。
words.en: Agony is very severe physical or mental pain.

words.ex: He felt deep misery after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到深深的痛苦。
words.en: Misery is a state of great unhappiness and emotional distress.

words.ex: He felt miserable after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到很悲惨。
words.en: If you are miserable, you are very unhappy.

words.tr:
adj. 警觉的；警惕的；
n. 警报；
v. （使）警惕；（使）戒备；
words.ex: The alert guard noticed the strange movement.
words.ex_cn: 这位警觉的警卫注意到了奇怪的动静。
words.en: If you are alert, you are paying full attention to things around you and are able to deal with anything that might happen.

words.tr:
n. 小心；警告；注意；
v. 警告；劝...小心；
words.ex: He drove with caution on the icy road.
words.ex_cn: 他在结冰的道路上小心驾驶。
words.en: Caution is care that you take in order to avoid possible danger or trouble.

words.ex: He was cautious when crossing the busy street.
words.ex_cn: 他过繁忙的街道时很小心。
words.en: If you are cautious, you are careful and avoid taking risks.

words.ex: Wear a helmet as a precaution when riding a bike.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔作为一种预防措施。
words.en: A precaution is an action that is intended to prevent something dangerous or unpleasant from happening.

words.tr: adj. 预防的；预先警戒的
words.ex: He took precautionary measures before the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他在风暴来临前采取了预防措施。
words.en: A precautionary action is taken in order to prevent something dangerous or unpleasant from happening.

words.ex: He won a trophy for first place in the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中获得第一名，赢得了一个奖杯。
words.en: A trophy is a prize, such as a gold or silver cup, that is given to the winner of a competition or race.

words.ex: The earthquake was a catastrophe.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场灾难。
words.en: An event causing great and often sudden damage or suffering; a disaster.

words.ex: The earthquake caused catastrophic damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了灾难性的破坏。
words.en: A catastrophic event or situation is one that causes great damage or suffering.

words.tr:
n. 上升；提高；
v. 上升；提高；
words.ex: There was a rise in temperature yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天温度上升了。
words.en: If an amount or level rises, it increases; if something rises, it moves upwards; if you rise, you stand up; if you rise, you get out of bed.

words.ex: A problem arose during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议中出现了一个问题。
words.en: If a situation or problem arises, it begins to exist or people start to become aware of it.

words.ex: The movie aroused his curiosity.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影激起了他的好奇心。
words.en: If something arouses a particular reaction or attitude in people, it causes them to have that reaction or attitude.

words.ex: The movie caused a strong arousal of emotions.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影唤起了强烈的情感。
words.en: Arousal is the state of being awake or of reacting to stimuli; it can also refer to the act of arousing someone or something.

words.tr: v. 增加；引起；筹募；提起；养育；
words.ex: The company will raise wages next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将提高工资。
words.en: To raise something means to move it to a higher position or to increase it in amount or level.

words.ex: The people started an uprising against the unfair rules.
words.ex_cn: 人们因不公平的规则而发动了起义。
words.en: An uprising is a violent act of opposition by many people in one area against those who are in power there.

words.ex: The team celebrated their victory after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，球队庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A victory is a success in a struggle, war, or competition.

words.ex: He felt victorious after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得比赛后感到胜利。
words.en: Having won a victory; conquering.

words.ex: The team celebrated their triumph after winning the match.
words.ex_cn: 球队在赢得比赛后庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.

words.ex: He was triumphant after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得比赛后非常成功。
words.en: If you are triumphant, you have achieved a great victory or success, often making you feel very proud and happy.

words.ex: He became the champion of the tennis tournament.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了网球锦标赛的冠军。
